Qualifying admission: the researcher rules list congressional reports as government admissions; the committee states the balance 'is justly due them' and the Creek demands 'should have been complied with'. Kept, with its committee-level weight noted.

Repayment: 1852 Indian appropriation act (10 Stat. 41 ff.) has no such item; Caselaw Access Project Creek Nation Court of Claims opinions (1927-1942) do not mention Indian Spring or the balance; Creek-Seminole treaty of Aug. 7, 1856 (11 Stat. 699) Article 5 releases all Creek claims not secured by existing treaties and laws, without naming this one.
OSU text: Jan. 8, 1821, 7 Stat. 215, proclaimed Mar. 2, 1821; 1,000 acres at Indian Spring, 640 acres on the Ocmulgee; fourteen payments in fourteen successive years; Georgia claims up to $250,000.
changes: Article 4 payment promise reworded: fourteen payments in all, including the first two (was 'then annual sums over fourteen years').
Compensation, openQuestions and plain.today now record that no repayment act was found and that the 1856 treaty released Creek claims in general terms.
unverifiable: The fate of S. No. 329 and the 1848 House report (H. Rpt. 826) on the same claim were not traced.
